subject: Partial throughput impact on hosted text-generation endpoints — notice and interim remediation
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: HaloHealth Ops <ops@halohealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop, ben_carter, evelyn_hart
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Notice: Partial throughput degradation affecting hosted text-generation endpoints

Hi Tom / HaloHealth team,

We want to make you aware of a partial service impact we began observing at ~08:45 PDT this morning that affects short-sequence text-generation requests on our hosted inference tier (your traffic routed to us in us-west-2). Customers may see higher queuing and reduced throughput, which has manifested as a 10–30% increase in P99 latency and occasional throttling on high-concurrency flows.

What we have done so far:
- Enabled emergency autoscale to add capacity to the affected pool.
- Activated per-customer fallback routing to alternate compatible model variants in a different pool/region where capacity was available.
- Added short-term rate smoothing on very small requests to reduce queue head-of-line blocking.

Impact: Some requests will retry or return slightly slower than usual; we do not believe model outputs themselves were affected.

Immediate ask for you: if you have any critical jobs (scheduled batch runs, demos) that need priority routing, reply to this thread and we'll pin routing for that customer while we stabilize.

We have created an incident record: INC-20260902 (https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-20260902). We'll post updates there and follow up with a full postmortem. Attaching a small log snippet and an initial timeline.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is bad timing for some customers and we're treating this as high priority.

— Rishi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_log_snippet.txt (excerpt)
From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@halohealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: HaloHealth Ops <ops@halohealth.com>, lauren_bishop
Date: 2026-09-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: Partial throughput degradation affecting hosted text-generation endpoints

Thanks for the heads up, Rishi. We're seeing the latency on our end as well starting ~08:50 PDT. Appreciate the quick mitigation steps — can you give an ETA on when you expect normal throughput to return? Also, if you need us to limit our spike traffic, we can throttle noncritical calls from our end for the next hour.

Tom
SRE, HaloHealth
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@halohealth.com>, HaloHealth Ops <ops@halohealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra, ben_carter, evelyn_hart
Date: 2026-09-02T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Infra update — queuing spike + kernel hotpath regression

Forwarding summary from infra: 

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Infra Alert <alerts@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:31:00-07:00
Subject: (Internal) Observed queuing spike — short-seq kernel miss

Summary:
- At 08:42 PDT we began seeing a workload shift with unusually high short-sequence synchronous calls that preferentially hit a newly-deployed kernel variant on a subset of GPU hosts.
- That kernel variant introduced a regression under high concurrency that increased per-request scheduling jitter; this caused queue head-of-line effects and reduced effective throughput for small requests.
- Rolling back the kernel on affected hosts is in progress; we are also diverting traffic to unaffected pools and applying temporary request smoothing.

Estimated time to full mitigation: 40–60 minutes from initial detection, depending on rollback propagation.

Attachments: timeline_20260902.csv

----- End forwarded message -----

Tom — we expect visible improvement within the next hour; we've already started the rollbacks and traffic diversion. We'll update the status page and this thread when throughput looks normal.

— Lauren
Senior Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@halohealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: HaloHealth Ops <ops@halohealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Infra update — queuing spike + kernel hotpath regression

Appreciate the rapid response — we are already observing fewer throttles and the P99 is trending back down. Two asks for the postmortem: 1) a timeline of the kernel rollout and rollback, and 2) retention of request-level logs for 72 hours for our audit team. Can you confirm those will be available?

If you can confirm, we won't escalate further from our side.

Tom
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@halohealth.com>, HaloHealth Ops <ops@halohealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop, ben_carter, evelyn_hart
Date: 2026-09-03T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: INC-20260902 — partial throughput impact (final)

Tom / HaloHealth team,

Thanks again for your patience. This is the final follow-up for INC-20260902. Key points: 

Root cause:
- A kernel variant deployed in us-west-2 had a performance regression under a specific high-concurrency, short-sequence profile. The regression increased internal scheduling jitter which generated queue head-of-line effects across the affected GPU hosts.

Blast radius and impact:
- Affected pool served a subset of hosted customers using the short-seq endpoints; typical symptom was elevated P99 latency (10–30%) and occasional request queuing that reduced throughput for high-concurrency flows. No model correctness issues were observed.

Mitigation and timeline (high level):
- 08:42 PDT: anomaly detected (queue growth).
- 08:50 PDT: emergency autoscale & traffic diversion started.
- 09:10 PDT: rollback of kernel variant began on affected hosts.
- 09:45 PDT: majority of hosts rolled back; visible P99/throughput improvement.
- 10:30 PDT: incident declared mitigated on status page.

Follow-up actions:
- Revert deployment gating to include concurrency-driven simulation tests and add a short-sequence stress test to our CI prior to kernel rollouts.
- Enhance post-deploy telemetry to detect head-of-line queue formation earlier.
- Provide retained logs and a full CSV timeline (attached) for your compliance team.

Attachments: postmortem-INC-20260902.pdf, timeline_20260902.csv
Related: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-20260902

We've uploaded request-level logs for the affected window and will retain them for 7 days; if you require a different retention window for compliance, let us know and we'll coordinate with our compliance team.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating the gating and telemetry fixes as high priority. If you'd like a short walkthrough of the postmortem with our infra leads, I'm available tomorrow morning PST.

— Rishi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
